items.title: Why do we let the AI companies dominate regulation discussion?
items.raw_excerpt:
And I don't mean the doomerism nonsense. From rogue AI, doomerism, AGI. I mean real regulation: 1) Fair accounting of input/output tokens. Where is the weights and measures department to enforce fair counting of usage? If I pay for a gallon of gas, that is what I expect. When I pay for a dollar of LLM compute, is it going to play games with the input (or especially the output) tokens to devalue my dollar?
2) Quality. items.title: Orglet, an open source desktop app for your own team of cute AI workers
items.raw_excerpt: I’m building Orglet, a desktop app where you give AI workers (I call them orglets, and they are cute) their own instructions and talk to them individually or together in a group chat. You can build your own army of orglets using your existing Claude Code or Codex subscription, an API provider, or even locally hosted models. Like other agent harnesses, orglets can access a working folder you give them permission to use. They can split the work among themselves, and you can review the resulting diff before applying changes to your files. Each orglet has its own role, tools and permissions. Orglet is free under AGPLv3. Downloads are available for Windows, macOS and Linux. It is still very early and flaky, so I’d appreciate any contributions. Thank you!
